terms.gloss: an engineer, a builder of machines
evidence: Liv. 24.34.2: inventor ac māchinātor bellicōrum tormentōrum, of Archimedes (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: A woman is māchinātrīx (Traupman 166). The word also means a contriver or schemer, often of crimes (hōrum omnium scelerum improbissimus māchinātor, Cic. Cat. 3.6), so the setting should make the trade clear.

evidence: Plaut. Mil. 3.3.45: fabrī architectīque; Cic. de Or. 1.62 (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: For the engineer who designs and oversees buildings, roads and bridges; also, figuratively, the author of a plan (Lewis & Short). See architect.
Pliny’s phrase for the knowledge of machines, of Archimedes (NH 7.125); Traupman gives it for engineering. Gellius has disciplīna mēchanica (see technology).

phrases.english: the inventor and builder of engines of war

phrases.latin: magistrī et māchinātōrēs, quibus ingenium et audācia erat
phrases.english: the master builders and engineers, who had the talent and the daring

sources: Lewis & Short: machinator · Lewis & Short: architectus · Lewis & Short: machinalis
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. mechanic: engineer.
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 166, 295, 310.
